unmatched.text: This also shaped an essay I wrote, *“Rise, Children of Utkal.”* I had heard the familiar expression “ଆମର ଏଠି କିଛି ହେବନି”—nothing will happen here. I understood that disappointment could sit behind it. Still, I wanted to leave the conversation open.[^utkal]

Music was present from the beginning. Bhuyan records fourteen songs in *Sita Bibah*, sung by its actors, and a move to background singing in *Lalita*. Later films drew on Odia literature, including *ଅମଡ଼ା ବାଟ (Amada Bata)*, *ମଲାଜହ୍ନ (Malajanha)* and *ମାଟିର ମଣିଷ (Matira Manisha)*.[^foundation]

Chhotray is a concrete link between the media. The Library of Congress documents his work in Gitinatya, his long association with AIR Cuttack, and his writing of plays, operas and screenplays.[^chhotray-loc] The Gour–Parbati archive credits him specifically with **dialogue for *ଶ୍ରୀଜଗନ୍ନାଥ (Sri Jagannath)* (1950)**, while assigning direction and screenplay to C.R. Mitra.[^jagannath-dialogue]

Parbati Ghose belongs near the centre of this history. The Gour–Parbati filmography records her as a co-producer with Gour Prasad Ghose on *ଲକ୍ଷ୍ମୀ (Laxmi)*, *କା (Kaa)* and *ସ୍ତ୍ରୀ (Stree)*. It also credits her within the directing partnership used on *Kaa* and *Stree*. Her work crossed the boundaries between performing, organising a production and deciding what would reach the screen.[^gour-parbati]

The archive dates her *ଛ’ ମାଣ ଆଠ ଗୁଣ୍ଠ (Chha Mana Atha Guntha)* adaptation to 1986. Its credits name **Nagen Barik** for sound and **Asim Basu and Sarat Sahoo** for art, and acknowledge Olosingh’s villagers and host **Kalyani Patnaik**.[^parbati-film] The [Parbati Ghose companion](cinema-series/parbati-ghose.md) follows her producing, writing, directing and acting work.

In his account of Odisha’s New Wave, critic Ashok Palit describes the social worlds of Mahapatra’s films: a rural community facing upheaval in *ନୀରବ ଝଡ଼ (Niraba Jhada)*, and a family negotiating social change in *ନିଷିଦ୍ଧ ସ୍ଵପ୍ନ (Nisiddha Swapna)*. His survey places Mahapatra and Nirad Mohapatra among the filmmakers who developed a sustained interest in cinema as an art of close observation.[^new-wave]

Sabyasachi Mohapatra’s *ଭୂଖା (Bhukha)* (**1989**) makes the map of cinema in Odisha more expansive. It is a **Sambalpuri-language film**. Palit reads its conflict through the pressures between inherited ways of life and modernity.[^new-wave]

Mohapatra’s later work offers further, separately documented milestones. *ଶଳାବୁଢ଼ା (Sala Budha)* was selected for Indian Panorama in 2013. *ଆଦିମ ବିଚାର (Aadim Vichar)* received the Best Odiya Film award at the 62nd National Film Awards, for 2014, announced in 2015.[^sala][^aadim]

Sadhu Meher’s ବାବୁଲା (Babula) provides a concrete starting point for the first history. A Lok Sabha answer of 7 December 1987 lists it among the Children’s Film Society of India’s productions for 1985–86, identifying it as an Oriya feature. A contemporary 1986 catalogue from Berlin’s Arsenal describes Meher’s CFSI-supported film through a lonely boy’s dreams of outer space. This places institutional support and a child’s imagination within the same account. [^children-babula-parliament][^children-babula-arsenal]

[A. K. Bir](../people/ak-bir.md)’s [ଲାବଣ୍ୟ ପ୍ରୀତି (Lavanya Preeti)](cinema-series/lavanya-preeti.md) received Best Children’s Film for 1993. Its dedicated page follows young characters into the imaginative world of an inherited story.[^children-lavanya-nfa]

Children can also encounter films through Odia-language versions. CBFC’s 2022 list records an Odia video version of ରିଟର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଅଫ୍ ହନୁମାନ (Return of Hanuman), certified on 11 February 2022 and naming Shemaroo Entertainment. Airtel Xstream lists the Anurag Kashyap film as a 2007 animation title available in Odia. This is a route to a dubbed film, distinct from an original Odia production; current access depends on the provider.[^children-hanuman-cbfc][^children-hanuman-provider]

Bijay Mohanty carried theatre training into films and into the classroom. A National School of Drama graduate, he worked in the drama department of Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya and retired as a professor. His screen career includes *ଚିଲିକା ତୀରେ (Chilika Tire)*, *ନାଗଫାଶ (Nagaphasa)* and *ଚକା ଭଉଁରୀ (Chaka Bhaunri)*: useful starting points for exploring a performer whose working life extended beyond the finished film.[^performer-bijay]

Uttam Mohanty's *ଅଭିମାନ (Abhiman)* debut connects his story to [Sadhu Meher](/cinema/sadhu-meher/), its director. In a 2018 interview, he recalled a Bengali viewer in Cuttack praising his portrayal of Salabega. The memory gives one audience encounter a place beside the career record.[^uttam-technology]

Aparajita Mohanty's work offers several points of entry. *ଉଦଣ୍ଡୀ ସୀତା (Udandi Sita)* is among the films associated with her screen career.[^performer-aparajita] She produced *Love Master*.[^performer-aparajita-production] Acting and producing are distinct forms of participation: one places a performer before the camera, while the other helps bring a production into being.

Her remembrance of Anita Das opens another relationship. Aparajita described the senior actor as an elder-sister figure who taught her about acting and the workings of the industry.[^performer-anita] That account gives mentorship between women a place in this history. Her later appearance in *ବୋଉ ବୁଟୁ ଭୂତ (Bou Buttu Bhuta)* brings that working life into the recent films discussed later in this survey.[^bou-commercial]
Her recollection of viewers calling her Manika, her character in *ଶେଷ ଶ୍ରାବଣ (Sesa Srabana)*, connects a role with audience memory.[^performer-mahasweta]

The credits of *ଶ୍ରୀ ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ (Sri Jagannath, 1950)* name **Balakrushna Das and Ranjit Roy** as music directors, with **Kalyani Das, Chhabi Ray and Suryamoni Dei** among the singers. Cinema was already a meeting place for many voices.[^music-sri-jagannath-archive] **Shantanu Mohapatra** later composed Lata Mangeshkar's songs for *ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟମୁଖୀ (Suryamukhi)* and *ଅରୁନ୍ଧତୀ (Arundhati)*. His son Koushik remembers a young composer approaching her, and producer Dhiren Patnaik backing the later collaboration. Such journeys began with someone making a connection and someone else making room for it.[^music-shantanu-lata]

[Akshaya Mohanty](../people/akshaya-mohanty.md) belongs here as a composer, singer and producer. When *ମଲାଜହ୍ନ (Malajanha)* returned for a Film Journalists' Forum screening, actress **Jharana Das**, singer [Pranab Patnaik](../people/pranab-patnaik.md), lyricist **Binodini Debi** and the filmmakers' families were part of the occasion. A literary adaptation had gathered actors, words and music; its return gathered people again.[^music-malajanha-return]

Other voices deserve their own listening paths. **Bhubaneswari Mishra's** “Tiki Mora Naa Ti” in *କୃଷ୍ଣ ସୁଦାମା (Krushna Sudama)* is one such doorway.[^music-bhubaneswari] Pranab Patnaik's account of his long friendship and stage work with Prafulla Kar offers another.[^music-pranab-remembers] These are starting points for a wider account of the singers, lyricists, arrangers and instrumentalists behind the songs.

**Sadhu Meher** received the National Film Award for Best Actor for his performance in Shyam Benegal’s Hindi film *ଅଙ୍କୁର (Ankur)*, honoured at the 22nd awards for 1974. The official catalogue records his upbringing in Odisha and his training at the Film and Television Institute in Pune. This is a major achievement by an actor from Odisha, within the history of Hindi cinema.[^sadhu]

Her connection also includes acting in Odia: she appeared in Susant Misra’s **ବିଶ୍ୱପ୍ରକାଶ (Biswaprakash / The Young Rebel, 1999)**, listed in her official filmography. The [Nandita Das article](/cinema/nandita-das/#acting-in-odia-biswaprakash) explores that credit alongside her wider career.[^nandita-acting]

Cannes records her membership of its feature-film jury in **2005** and its Cinéfondation and short-film jury in **2013**. Her film *ମଣ୍ଟୋ (Manto)* was selected for Un Certain Regard in **2018**. These occasions mark both jury service and film selection across her career in acting and directing.[^nandita-cannes]
[ଲାବଣ୍ୟ ପ୍ରୀତି (Lavanya Preeti)](cinema-series/lavanya-preeti.md)
[ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)](cinema-series/pratikshya.md)

Recognition also follows people across languages. [Sadhu Meher](cinema-series/sadhu-meher.md) received Best Actor for *ଅଙ୍କୁର (Ankur)* at the 22nd awards for 1974. His achievement belongs here as an actor from Odisha working in a Hindi film.[^sadhu]

**A Sambalpuri film’s recognition abroad:** the official 70th National Film Awards catalogue credits [ଭୂଖା (Bhukha)](cinema-series/bhukha.md) with an **International Jury Award at Gijón, Spain**. The catalogue does not give the prize year; that detail remains open for further archive research.[^bhukha]

The newer *ମାଲିପୁଟ (Maliput Melodies)* was screened in **Indian Panorama at IFFI 2025**. That documented festival appearance opens a contemporary thread below; it is kept distinct from the prize record.[^maliput-iffi]

A film can leave something behind after its run: a new collaborator, an audience willing to try another story, or the confidence to begin a difficult script. *ଦମନ (DAMaN)* and *ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)* offer two recent starting points for that conversation. Their subjects are different—healthcare in a difficult landscape, and the pressures inside a household—but both give recognisably local lives room on the screen.

The range also includes **କର୍ମ (Karma, 2024)**. Anupam Patnaik directed **Anubhav Mohanty** as investigator Amar Patnaik in a murder-case thriller. The filmmaker behind *Pratikshya* was working with a different star and dramatic form; contemporary Odia cinema cannot be reduced to a single kind of revival.[^karma-contemporary]

A film culture also depends on tickets sold and the chance to finance the next production. In 2025, **ବୋଉ ବୁଟୁ ଭୂତ (Bou Buttu Bhuta)** supplied a conspicuous commercial story. Directed by **Jagdish Mishra**, the horror-comedy brought **Aparajita Mohanty, Babushaan Mohanty and Archita Sahu** together in leading roles. On 24 September 2025, *The New Indian Express* reported box-office revenue of nearly **₹21 crore**, against a reported budget of **₹2–3 crore**. These are reported figures, not audited accounts or a calculation of producer profit.[^bou-commercial]

Commercial momentum has a setting as well as a number. During Raja in June 2025, *The New Indian Express* reported packed shows for *Bou Buttu Bhuta* and **ଅନନ୍ତା (Ananta)**. The latter starred **Sabyasachi Mishra** and was directed by **Sabyasachi Mohapatra**, drawing on Fakir Mohan Senapati’s *Randi Pua Ananta*. Literature and popular exhibition were meeting again.[^raja-audiences]

Overseas announcements show another route to audiences. On 26 April 2023, *OrissaPOST* reported plans to screen **ଫାଲ୍ଗୁନ ଚୈତ୍ର (Phalguna Chaitra)** on 13 May at Hoyts Docklands in Melbourne, Hoyts Blacktown in Sydney and Event Cinemas in Brisbane. A July follow-up in *OrissaPOST* subsequently reported overseas screenings, including Australia. Neither report supplied receipts or a country-by-country earnings breakdown.[^phalgun-australia][^phalgun-followup]

In the chapter “Bhagia and Saria” of ଛମାଣ ଆଠଗୁଣ୍ଠ (Chha Mana Atha Guntha), Fakir Mohan Senapati’s narrator turns towards educated readers who know distant societies better than their neighbours. The question is deliberately ironic:
“ଆପଣାର ବା ପ୍ରତିବାସୀ ଜାତି ଓ ସମାଜର କଥା ଜାଣିବାର ଦରକାର କ'ଣ ?”
In the opening household passage of ରେବତୀ (Rebati), Fakir Mohan describes a child beside her father as he reads and sings:
“ରେବତୀ ପାଖରେ ବସି ଶୁଣୁଥାଏ।”

Pratibha Ray’s official bibliography identifies her novel ଅପରିଚିତା (Aparichita) as adapted into a film and the title story of ମୋକ୍ଷ (Moksha) as adapted into a feature.[^pratibha] A novel’s sustained companionship and a short story’s concentrated moment offer different possibilities to the screen.

Other paths lead through theatre and contemporary short fiction. ଭୂଖା (Bhukha) grew from Manglu Charan Biswal’s play, bringing folk performers’ livelihoods into a Sambalpuri screen story.[^lit-bhukha] [ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)](pratikshya.md) draws on a short story by [Gourahari Das](../../people/gourahari-das.md).[^lit-pratikshya] BookMyShow’s listing for ଅନନ୍ତା (Ananta) identifies Fakir Mohan’s *Randi Pua Ananta* as its literary source.[^lit-ananta]

Odia Bibhaba’s collection identifies ଶ୍ରୀମତୀ ସମାର୍ଜନୀ (Srimati Samarjani) as Chhotray’s opera adaptation of Fakir Mohan Senapati’s short story *Patent Medicine*.[^archive] A work of fiction had become something that singers and performers could take up together.

In ଶ୍ରୀଜଗନ୍ନାଥ (Sri Jagannath, 1950), the Gour–Parbati archive credits Chhotray for dialogue and C.R. Mitra for screenplay and direction.[^jagannath] For ମାଆ (Maa), Chhotray shares the dialogue credit with Biswajit Das; Nitai Palit is credited with screenplay and direction.[^maa]

His connection with cinema can be made precise. The Gour–Parbati film archive credits him with dialogue for **ଶ୍ରୀଜଗନ୍ନାଥ (Sri Jagannath, 1950)**. The same record names C.R. Mitra for direction and screenplay.[^jagannath]
Odia Bibhaba’s Chhotray collection identifies **ଶ୍ରୀମତୀ ସମାର୍ଜନୀ (Srimati Samarjani)** as an opera adapted from Fakir Mohan Senapati’s short story *Patent Medicine*.[^bibhaba]
**Bhubaneswari Mishra** offers another starting point with “Tiki Mora Naa Ti” in *କୃଷ୍ଣ ସୁଦାମା (Krushna Sudama)*.[^bhubaneswari]

Her voice also meets **Humane Sagar’s** in the title song of *ଇସ୍କ ତୁ ହି ତୁ (Ishq Tu Hi Tu)*. The recording credits both singers, **Abhijit Majumdar** as composer and **Nizam** as writer.[^ishq] Reporting on Sagar’s career identifies the 2015 film’s title track as a breakthrough.[^humane] Listening through the duet keeps both performers in view, together with the people who supplied its music and words.

**Aseema Panda’s** training began with Odissi music under Prafulla Kumar Sahoo, followed by Hindustani music under Artatrana Bhola. In her account, that learning sits beside the film work for which she received state best-singer recognition, *ମୁଁ ଖାଣ୍ଟି ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଝିଅ (Mu Khanti Odia Jhia)*.[^aseema]
**Diptirekha Padhi** and **Sabisesh Mishra** share “Bhala Paigali Tate” from *ତୁ ମୋ ଲଭ୍ ଷ୍ଟୋରୀ-୨ (Tu Mo Love Story 2)*, as the official Tarang Music recording credits show.[^diptirekha]
Tarang Music, [“Bhala Paigali Tate”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2rLxCCFVqs), *ତୁ ମୋ ଲଭ୍ ଷ୍ଟୋରୀ-୨ (Tu Mo Love Story 2)* recording credits.

In a public caption headed “ଲୋକସ୍ୱର ଛାଞ୍ଚ”, film historian Surya Deo discusses a duet by Akshaya Mohanty and **Trupti Das**, with lyrics by **Sirshananda Das Kanungo**. Deo draws attention to a folk-shaped pattern of question, answer and retort, and to a simple, expressive delivery.[^folk-exchange] His account directs attention to something shared: the lyric creates an exchange, and two singers carry it.

Mohanty entered cinema as a playback singer in **ମାଆ (Maa)** in the late 1950s, under composer **Bhubaneswar Mishra**, alongside fellow playback singers **Pranab Patnaik** and **Ila Chakraborty**.[^maa] By **ମଲାଜହ୍ନ (Malajanha, 1965)**, he was its music director.[^malajanha] A voice heard within a film was now helping shape its musical world.
Surya Deo, [“ଲୋକସ୍ୱର ଛାଞ୍ଚ”](https://www.facebook.com/reel/28591660633830620/), public Facebook caption.

Kar entered film playback with *ଶ୍ରୀ ଶ୍ରୀ ପତିତପାବନ (Shri Shri Patita Pabana)* in 1962 and made his debut as a film music director with *ମମତା (Mamata)* in 1975.[^career] These were different responsibilities within the same musical world: singing a part and shaping music for a production.

Kar’s own voice offers another route. The distributed soundtrack listing for *ଶେଷ ଶ୍ରାବଣ (Sesa Srabana)* credits him as composer and main artist for “Kali Kapali.”[^kali] Here the person shaping the music is also named as its performer.

Mishra grew up in Sambalpur and began singing young. She attended Sambalpur University and obtained a music degree from Gandharva Mahavidyalaya. Her film career began with Himanshu Parija’s *କୁଳନନ୍ଦନ (Kulanandana)* in 1995; “Na Re Na Bajana Bansi” from *ଆଇ ଲଭ୍ ୟୁ (I Love You)* brought her wider recognition.[^career]

Tapu and Humane Sagar shared the title song of *ଇସ୍କ ତୁ ହି ତୁ (Ishq Tu Hi Tu)*. Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and Nizam wrote the words.[^ishq] The recording places her within a newer chapter of the [Odia cinema-music story](../culture/cinema-series/cinema-music.md), alongside a fellow singer whose voice also became closely associated with contemporary film songs.

The archive’s filmography records Gour and Parbati across productions including *ଲକ୍ଷ୍ମୀ (Laxmi)*, *କା (Kaa)* and *ସ୍ତ୍ରୀ (Stree)*. For the latter two, it identifies the directing name **Siddharth** with **Ram Chandra Thakur, Gour and Parbati**.[^credits] That collective credit should remain visible rather than being reassigned to one person.

# ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya): a family waiting for security

A secure job can become more than employment. It can stand for a family’s hopes, the ability to repay a loan and relief from being dependent on someone else. **ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)** places that desire beside a father’s illness, until the son’s hope for security becomes entangled with the possibility of loss.

Seventeen drafts and three years of work: that is how Anupam Patnaik described making *ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)*. unmatched.text: This also shaped an essay I wrote, *“Rise, Children of Utkal.”* I had heard the familiar expression “ଆମର ଏଠି କିଛି ହେବନି”—nothing will happen here. I understood that disappointment could sit behind it. Still, I wanted to leave the conversation open.[^utkal]

Music was present from the beginning. Bhuyan records fourteen songs in *Sita Bibah*, sung by its actors, and a move to background singing in *Lalita*. Later films drew on Odia literature, including *ଅମଡ଼ା ବାଟ (Amada Bata)*, *ମଲାଜହ୍ନ (Malajanha)* and *ମାଟିର ମଣିଷ (Matira Manisha)*.[^foundation]

Chhotray is a concrete link between the media. The Library of Congress documents his work in Gitinatya, his long association with AIR Cuttack, and his writing of plays, operas and screenplays.[^chhotray-loc] The Gour–Parbati archive credits him specifically with **dialogue for *ଶ୍ରୀଜଗନ୍ନାଥ (Sri Jagannath)* (1950)**, while assigning direction and screenplay to C.R. Mitra.[^jagannath-dialogue]

Parbati Ghose belongs near the centre of this history. The Gour–Parbati filmography records her as a co-producer with Gour Prasad Ghose on *ଲକ୍ଷ୍ମୀ (Laxmi)*, *କା (Kaa)* and *ସ୍ତ୍ରୀ (Stree)*. It also credits her within the directing partnership used on *Kaa* and *Stree*. Her work crossed the boundaries between performing, organising a production and deciding what would reach the screen.[^gour-parbati]

The archive dates her *ଛ’ ମାଣ ଆଠ ଗୁଣ୍ଠ (Chha Mana Atha Guntha)* adaptation to 1986. Its credits name **Nagen Barik** for sound and **Asim Basu and Sarat Sahoo** for art, and acknowledge Olosingh’s villagers and host **Kalyani Patnaik**.[^parbati-film] The [Parbati Ghose companion](cinema-series/parbati-ghose.md) follows her producing, writing, directing and acting work.

In his account of Odisha’s New Wave, critic Ashok Palit describes the social worlds of Mahapatra’s films: a rural community facing upheaval in *ନୀରବ ଝଡ଼ (Niraba Jhada)*, and a family negotiating social change in *ନିଷିଦ୍ଧ ସ୍ଵପ୍ନ (Nisiddha Swapna)*. His survey places Mahapatra and Nirad Mohapatra among the filmmakers who developed a sustained interest in cinema as an art of close observation.[^new-wave]

Sabyasachi Mohapatra’s *ଭୂଖା (Bhukha)* (**1989**) makes the map of cinema in Odisha more expansive. It is a **Sambalpuri-language film**. Palit reads its conflict through the pressures between inherited ways of life and modernity.[^new-wave]

Mohapatra’s later work offers further, separately documented milestones. *ଶଳାବୁଢ଼ା (Sala Budha)* was selected for Indian Panorama in 2013. *ଆଦିମ ବିଚାର (Aadim Vichar)* received the Best Odiya Film award at the 62nd National Film Awards, for 2014, announced in 2015.[^sala][^aadim]

Sadhu Meher’s ବାବୁଲା (Babula) provides a concrete starting point for the first history. A Lok Sabha answer of 7 December 1987 lists it among the Children’s Film Society of India’s productions for 1985–86, identifying it as an Oriya feature. A contemporary 1986 catalogue from Berlin’s Arsenal describes Meher’s CFSI-supported film through a lonely boy’s dreams of outer space. This places institutional support and a child’s imagination within the same account. [^children-babula-parliament][^children-babula-arsenal]

[A. K. Bir](../people/ak-bir.md)’s [ଲାବଣ୍ୟ ପ୍ରୀତି (Lavanya Preeti)](cinema-series/lavanya-preeti.md) received Best Children’s Film for 1993. Its dedicated page follows young characters into the imaginative world of an inherited story.[^children-lavanya-nfa]

Children can also encounter films through Odia-language versions. CBFC’s 2022 list records an Odia video version of ରିଟର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଅଫ୍ ହନୁମାନ (Return of Hanuman), certified on 11 February 2022 and naming Shemaroo Entertainment. Airtel Xstream lists the Anurag Kashyap film as a 2007 animation title available in Odia. This is a route to a dubbed film, distinct from an original Odia production; current access depends on the provider.[^children-hanuman-cbfc][^children-hanuman-provider]

Bijay Mohanty carried theatre training into films and into the classroom. A National School of Drama graduate, he worked in the drama department of Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya and retired as a professor. His screen career includes *ଚିଲିକା ତୀରେ (Chilika Tire)*, *ନାଗଫାଶ (Nagaphasa)* and *ଚକା ଭଉଁରୀ (Chaka Bhaunri)*: useful starting points for exploring a performer whose working life extended beyond the finished film.[^performer-bijay]

Uttam Mohanty's *ଅଭିମାନ (Abhiman)* debut connects his story to [Sadhu Meher](/cinema/sadhu-meher/), its director. In a 2018 interview, he recalled a Bengali viewer in Cuttack praising his portrayal of Salabega. The memory gives one audience encounter a place beside the career record.[^uttam-technology]

Aparajita Mohanty's work offers several points of entry. *ଉଦଣ୍ଡୀ ସୀତା (Udandi Sita)* is among the films associated with her screen career.[^performer-aparajita] She produced *Love Master*.[^performer-aparajita-production] Acting and producing are distinct forms of participation: one places a performer before the camera, while the other helps bring a production into being.

Her remembrance of Anita Das opens another relationship. Aparajita described the senior actor as an elder-sister figure who taught her about acting and the workings of the industry.[^performer-anita] That account gives mentorship between women a place in this history. Her later appearance in *ବୋଉ ବୁଟୁ ଭୂତ (Bou Buttu Bhuta)* brings that working life into the recent films discussed later in this survey.[^bou-commercial]
Her recollection of viewers calling her Manika, her character in *ଶେଷ ଶ୍ରାବଣ (Sesa Srabana)*, connects a role with audience memory.[^performer-mahasweta]

The credits of *ଶ୍ରୀ ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ (Sri Jagannath, 1950)* name **Balakrushna Das and Ranjit Roy** as music directors, with **Kalyani Das, Chhabi Ray and Suryamoni Dei** among the singers. Cinema was already a meeting place for many voices.[^music-sri-jagannath-archive] **Shantanu Mohapatra** later composed Lata Mangeshkar's songs for *ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟମୁଖୀ (Suryamukhi)* and *ଅରୁନ୍ଧତୀ (Arundhati)*. His son Koushik remembers a young composer approaching her, and producer Dhiren Patnaik backing the later collaboration. Such journeys began with someone making a connection and someone else making room for it.[^music-shantanu-lata]

[Akshaya Mohanty](../people/akshaya-mohanty.md) belongs here as a composer, singer and producer. When *ମଲାଜହ୍ନ (Malajanha)* returned for a Film Journalists' Forum screening, actress **Jharana Das**, singer [Pranab Patnaik](../people/pranab-patnaik.md), lyricist **Binodini Debi** and the filmmakers' families were part of the occasion. A literary adaptation had gathered actors, words and music; its return gathered people again.[^music-malajanha-return]

Other voices deserve their own listening paths. **Bhubaneswari Mishra's** “Tiki Mora Naa Ti” in *କୃଷ୍ଣ ସୁଦାମା (Krushna Sudama)* is one such doorway.[^music-bhubaneswari] Pranab Patnaik's account of his long friendship and stage work with Prafulla Kar offers another.[^music-pranab-remembers] These are starting points for a wider account of the singers, lyricists, arrangers and instrumentalists behind the songs.

**Sadhu Meher** received the National Film Award for Best Actor for his performance in Shyam Benegal’s Hindi film *ଅଙ୍କୁର (Ankur)*, honoured at the 22nd awards for 1974. The official catalogue records his upbringing in Odisha and his training at the Film and Television Institute in Pune. This is a major achievement by an actor from Odisha, within the history of Hindi cinema.[^sadhu]

Her connection also includes acting in Odia: she appeared in Susant Misra’s **ବିଶ୍ୱପ୍ରକାଶ (Biswaprakash / The Young Rebel, 1999)**, listed in her official filmography. The [Nandita Das article](/cinema/nandita-das/#acting-in-odia-biswaprakash) explores that credit alongside her wider career.[^nandita-acting]

Cannes records her membership of its feature-film jury in **2005** and its Cinéfondation and short-film jury in **2013**. Her film *ମଣ୍ଟୋ (Manto)* was selected for Un Certain Regard in **2018**. These occasions mark both jury service and film selection across her career in acting and directing.[^nandita-cannes]

Recognition also follows people across languages. [Sadhu Meher](cinema-series/sadhu-meher.md) received Best Actor for *ଅଙ୍କୁର (Ankur)* at the 22nd awards for 1974. His achievement belongs here as an actor from Odisha working in a Hindi film.[^sadhu]

**A Sambalpuri film’s recognition abroad:** the official 70th National Film Awards catalogue credits [ଭୂଖା (Bhukha)](cinema-series/bhukha.md) with an **International Jury Award at Gijón, Spain**. The catalogue does not give the prize year; that detail remains open for further archive research.[^bhukha]

The newer *ମାଲିପୁଟ (Maliput Melodies)* was screened in **Indian Panorama at IFFI 2025**. That documented festival appearance opens a contemporary thread below; it is kept distinct from the prize record.[^maliput-iffi]

A film can leave something behind after its run: a new collaborator, an audience willing to try another story, or the confidence to begin a difficult script. *ଦମନ (DAMaN)* and *ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)* offer two recent starting points for that conversation. Their subjects are different—healthcare in a difficult landscape, and the pressures inside a household—but both give recognisably local lives room on the screen.

The range also includes **କର୍ମ (Karma, 2024)**. Anupam Patnaik directed **Anubhav Mohanty** as investigator Amar Patnaik in a murder-case thriller. The filmmaker behind *Pratikshya* was working with a different star and dramatic form; contemporary Odia cinema cannot be reduced to a single kind of revival.[^karma-contemporary]

A film culture also depends on tickets sold and the chance to finance the next production. In 2025, **ବୋଉ ବୁଟୁ ଭୂତ (Bou Buttu Bhuta)** supplied a conspicuous commercial story. Directed by **Jagdish Mishra**, the horror-comedy brought **Aparajita Mohanty, Babushaan Mohanty and Archita Sahu** together in leading roles. On 24 September 2025, *The New Indian Express* reported box-office revenue of nearly **₹21 crore**, against a reported budget of **₹2–3 crore**. These are reported figures, not audited accounts or a calculation of producer profit.[^bou-commercial]

Commercial momentum has a setting as well as a number. During Raja in June 2025, *The New Indian Express* reported packed shows for *Bou Buttu Bhuta* and **ଅନନ୍ତା (Ananta)**. The latter starred **Sabyasachi Mishra** and was directed by **Sabyasachi Mohapatra**, drawing on Fakir Mohan Senapati’s *Randi Pua Ananta*. Literature and popular exhibition were meeting again.[^raja-audiences]

Overseas announcements show another route to audiences. On 26 April 2023, *OrissaPOST* reported plans to screen **ଫାଲ୍ଗୁନ ଚୈତ୍ର (Phalguna Chaitra)** on 13 May at Hoyts Docklands in Melbourne, Hoyts Blacktown in Sydney and Event Cinemas in Brisbane. A July follow-up in *OrissaPOST* subsequently reported overseas screenings, including Australia. Neither report supplied receipts or a country-by-country earnings breakdown.[^phalgun-australia][^phalgun-followup]

In the chapter “Bhagia and Saria” of ଛମାଣ ଆଠଗୁଣ୍ଠ (Chha Mana Atha Guntha), Fakir Mohan Senapati’s narrator turns towards educated readers who know distant societies better than their neighbours. The question is deliberately ironic:
“ଆପଣାର ବା ପ୍ରତିବାସୀ ଜାତି ଓ ସମାଜର କଥା ଜାଣିବାର ଦରକାର କ'ଣ ?”
In the opening household passage of ରେବତୀ (Rebati), Fakir Mohan describes a child beside her father as he reads and sings:
“ରେବତୀ ପାଖରେ ବସି ଶୁଣୁଥାଏ।”

Pratibha Ray’s official bibliography identifies her novel ଅପରିଚିତା (Aparichita) as adapted into a film and the title story of ମୋକ୍ଷ (Moksha) as adapted into a feature.[^pratibha] A novel’s sustained companionship and a short story’s concentrated moment offer different possibilities to the screen.

Other paths lead through theatre and contemporary short fiction. ଭୂଖା (Bhukha) grew from Manglu Charan Biswal’s play, bringing folk performers’ livelihoods into a Sambalpuri screen story.[^lit-bhukha] [ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)](pratikshya.md) draws on a short story by [Gourahari Das](../../people/gourahari-das.md).[^lit-pratikshya] BookMyShow’s listing for ଅନନ୍ତା (Ananta) identifies Fakir Mohan’s *Randi Pua Ananta* as its literary source.[^lit-ananta]

Odia Bibhaba’s collection identifies ଶ୍ରୀମତୀ ସମାର୍ଜନୀ (Srimati Samarjani) as Chhotray’s opera adaptation of Fakir Mohan Senapati’s short story *Patent Medicine*.[^archive] A work of fiction had become something that singers and performers could take up together.

In ଶ୍ରୀଜଗନ୍ନାଥ (Sri Jagannath, 1950), the Gour–Parbati archive credits Chhotray for dialogue and C.R. Mitra for screenplay and direction.[^jagannath] For ମାଆ (Maa), Chhotray shares the dialogue credit with Biswajit Das; Nitai Palit is credited with screenplay and direction.[^maa]

His connection with cinema can be made precise. The Gour–Parbati film archive credits him with dialogue for **ଶ୍ରୀଜଗନ୍ନାଥ (Sri Jagannath, 1950)**. The same record names C.R. Mitra for direction and screenplay.[^jagannath]
Odia Bibhaba’s Chhotray collection identifies **ଶ୍ରୀମତୀ ସମାର୍ଜନୀ (Srimati Samarjani)** as an opera adapted from Fakir Mohan Senapati’s short story *Patent Medicine*.[^bibhaba]
**Bhubaneswari Mishra** offers another starting point with “Tiki Mora Naa Ti” in *କୃଷ୍ଣ ସୁଦାମା (Krushna Sudama)*.[^bhubaneswari]

Her voice also meets **Humane Sagar’s** in the title song of *ଇସ୍କ ତୁ ହି ତୁ (Ishq Tu Hi Tu)*. The recording credits both singers, **Abhijit Majumdar** as composer and **Nizam** as writer.[^ishq] Reporting on Sagar’s career identifies the 2015 film’s title track as a breakthrough.[^humane] Listening through the duet keeps both performers in view, together with the people who supplied its music and words.

**Aseema Panda’s** training began with Odissi music under Prafulla Kumar Sahoo, followed by Hindustani music under Artatrana Bhola. In her account, that learning sits beside the film work for which she received state best-singer recognition, *ମୁଁ ଖାଣ୍ଟି ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଝିଅ (Mu Khanti Odia Jhia)*.[^aseema]
**Diptirekha Padhi** and **Sabisesh Mishra** share “Bhala Paigali Tate” from *ତୁ ମୋ ଲଭ୍ ଷ୍ଟୋରୀ-୨ (Tu Mo Love Story 2)*, as the official Tarang Music recording credits show.[^diptirekha]
Tarang Music, [“Bhala Paigali Tate”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r2rLxCCFVqs), *ତୁ ମୋ ଲଭ୍ ଷ୍ଟୋରୀ-୨ (Tu Mo Love Story 2)* recording credits.

In a public caption headed “ଲୋକସ୍ୱର ଛାଞ୍ଚ”, film historian Surya Deo discusses a duet by Akshaya Mohanty and **Trupti Das**, with lyrics by **Sirshananda Das Kanungo**. Deo draws attention to a folk-shaped pattern of question, answer and retort, and to a simple, expressive delivery.[^folk-exchange] His account directs attention to something shared: the lyric creates an exchange, and two singers carry it.

Mohanty entered cinema as a playback singer in **ମାଆ (Maa)** in the late 1950s, under composer **Bhubaneswar Mishra**, alongside fellow playback singers **Pranab Patnaik** and **Ila Chakraborty**.[^maa] By **ମଲାଜହ୍ନ (Malajanha, 1965)**, he was its music director.[^malajanha] A voice heard within a film was now helping shape its musical world.
Surya Deo, [“ଲୋକସ୍ୱର ଛାଞ୍ଚ”](https://www.facebook.com/reel/28591660633830620/), public Facebook caption.

Kar entered film playback with *ଶ୍ରୀ ଶ୍ରୀ ପତିତପାବନ (Shri Shri Patita Pabana)* in 1962 and made his debut as a film music director with *ମମତା (Mamata)* in 1975.[^career] These were different responsibilities within the same musical world: singing a part and shaping music for a production.

Kar’s own voice offers another route. The distributed soundtrack listing for *ଶେଷ ଶ୍ରାବଣ (Sesa Srabana)* credits him as composer and main artist for “Kali Kapali.”[^kali] Here the person shaping the music is also named as its performer.

Mishra grew up in Sambalpur and began singing young. She attended Sambalpur University and obtained a music degree from Gandharva Mahavidyalaya. Her film career began with Himanshu Parija’s *କୁଳନନ୍ଦନ (Kulanandana)* in 1995; “Na Re Na Bajana Bansi” from *ଆଇ ଲଭ୍ ୟୁ (I Love You)* brought her wider recognition.[^career]

Tapu and Humane Sagar shared the title song of *ଇସ୍କ ତୁ ହି ତୁ (Ishq Tu Hi Tu)*. Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and Nizam wrote the words.[^ishq] The recording places her within a newer chapter of the [Odia cinema-music story](../culture/cinema-series/cinema-music.md), alongside a fellow singer whose voice also became closely associated with contemporary film songs.

The archive’s filmography records Gour and Parbati across productions including *ଲକ୍ଷ୍ମୀ (Laxmi)*, *କା (Kaa)* and *ସ୍ତ୍ରୀ (Stree)*. For the latter two, it identifies the directing name **Siddharth** with **Ram Chandra Thakur, Gour and Parbati**.[^credits] That collective credit should remain visible rather than being reassigned to one person.

[Parbati’s own profile](../culture/cinema-series/parbati-ghose.md) follows her producing, writing, directing and performance work, including *ଛ’ ମାଣ ଆଠ ଗୁଣ୍ଠ (Chha Mana Atha Guntha)*. Their partnership belongs in both lives, without making either career merely an appendix to the other.

In the published credits for *ଛ’ ମାଣ ଆଠ ଗୁଣ୍ଠ (Chha Mana Atha Guntha)*, Parbati Ghose appears as producer, director and performer. The screenplay and dialogue are credited to Shrabani, identified there as Parbati Ghose. The archive dates this adaptation of Fakir Mohan Senapati’s novel to 1986.[^adaptation]

The Gour–Parbati archive records her as co-producer with Gour Prasad Ghose on *ଲକ୍ଷ୍ମୀ (Laxmi)*, *କା (Kaa)* and *ସ୍ତ୍ରୀ (Stree)*. It also identifies “Siddharth,” the directing credit associated with *Kaa* and *Stree*, as a collaboration involving Ram Chandra Thakur, Gour and Parbati.[^filmography]

Kishtaya comes back to the village with money he has earned. Seeking work from Surya, the landlord’s son, he is beaten; his wife Lakshmi intervenes. # ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya): a family waiting for security

A secure job can become more than employment. It can stand for a family’s hopes, the ability to repay a loan and relief from being dependent on someone else. **ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)** places that desire beside a father’s illness, until the son’s hope for security becomes entangled with the possibility of loss.

Seventeen drafts and three years of work: that is how Anupam Patnaik described making *ପ୍ରତୀକ୍ଷା (Pratikshya)*. In an interview before its release, he recalled working with screenwriter Roshan Bisoi to find the shape of a story about a son, an ailing father and the longing for a secure job.[^drafts] The title means waiting. Behind the finished film was another kind of patience—the repeated work of returning to a story until it could be filmed.
